source_standard: current practice documentation with explicit provenance boundaries

sources.exact_title: Quality Control Charts
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 593–603; DOI landing abstract
sources.claim_supported: Introduces a charting method for detecting departures from statistical control in manufacturing quality.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct historical basis for P015–P021 and P059.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A chart signal is diagnostic evidence of non-random behaviour, not identification of a causal mechanism.

sources.exact_title: Economic Control of Quality of Manufactured Product
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: entire monograph; especially the economic-control and assignable-cause/control-chart chapters
sources.claim_supported: Frames quality control as economic control under variation and distinguishes chance from assignable causes.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct historical basis for statistical quality control and economic proportionality.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The original industrial setting does not validate indiscriminate transfer to every data-generating process.

sources.exact_title: Statistical Method from the Viewpoint of Quality Control
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. I–IV; discussion of prediction, statistical control, and scientific method
sources.claim_supported: Presents statistical control as a basis for prediction and an iterative scientific method, not merely a chart recipe.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct historical basis for P015, P020, P035, P056.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Its philosophical claims remain conditional on an adequate process model and measurement system.

sources.exact_title: How Did Statistical Quality Control Begin?
sources.claim_supported: Documents Shewhart’s Bell Labs role and the 1924 control-chart origin.
sources.relation_to_property: Historical corroboration for P015 and the timeline.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Concise institutional history; not a substitute for the primary works.

sources.exact_title: The Arrangement of Field Experiments
sources.date_version_edition: 1926; Journal of the Ministry of Agriculture 33:503–513
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article; DOI repository record and article pages 503–513
sources.claim_supported: Links randomisation, replication, local control/blocking and valid error assessment in experiment arrangement.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Agricultural field conditions differ from many industrial and online systems; transfer requires defining units and interference.

sources.exact_title: The Design of Experiments
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. II–IV on principles of experimentation; later chapters on factorial experiments
sources.claim_supported: Codifies randomisation, replication, blocking and factorial experimentation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Fisherian tests alone do not supply decision costs, external validity, or modern multiplicity/sequential safeguards.

sources.author_organisation: Jerzy Neyman and Egon S. Pearson
sources.exact_title: On the Problem of the Most Efficient Tests of Statistical Hypotheses
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 289–337; especially the formulation of alternatives and error probabilities
sources.claim_supported: Establishes a decision-oriented framework balancing error probabilities against specified alternatives.
sources.relation_to_property: Shared statistical ancestry for acceptance decisions, power, and P028–P029.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The framework does not itself determine engineering loss, practical importance, or whether model assumptions hold.

sources.author_organisation: Harold F. Dodge and Harry G. Romig
sources.exact_title: Sampling Inspection Tables: Single and Double Sampling
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: tables and introductory operating-characteristic discussion
sources.claim_supported: Operationalises lot acceptance under producer/consumer risk and inspection cost.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Lot disposition does not estimate process quality well and can become a substitute for prevention.

sources.author_organisation: George E. P. Box and K. B. Wilson
sources.exact_title: On the Experimental Attainment of Optimum Conditions
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 1–45
sources.claim_supported: Introduces sequential response-surface experimentation for moving toward an operating optimum.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct lineage for P035 and P041.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Local polynomial approximation and extrapolation can fail outside the explored region or under drift.

sources.author_organisation: R. L. Plackett and J. P. Burman
sources.exact_title: The Design of Optimum Multifactorial Experiments
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 305–325
sources.claim_supported: Provides economical screening designs for many factors.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Low-resolution screening aliases effects; interactions can contaminate apparent main effects.

sources.exact_title: Sequential Analysis
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. 1–4 on SPRT and operating characteristics
sources.claim_supported: Formalises planned sequential decisions with controlled error probabilities and expected sample-size advantages.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Applies to specified models and boundaries; unplanned optional stopping is not legitimised by the existence of sequential methods.

sources.exact_title: Optimum Character of the Sequential Probability Ratio Test
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Theorem and article pp. 326–339
sources.claim_supported: Shows optimality properties of SPRT under stated simple-hypothesis conditions.
sources.relation_to_property: Formal support for planned sequential evidence.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Optimality is model- and criterion-specific and does not generalise to arbitrary adaptive engineering review.

sources.exact_title: Continuous Inspection Schemes
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 100–115
sources.claim_supported: Introduces cumulative-sum monitoring for persistent shifts.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct evolution of process monitoring for P021–P024.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Sensitivity depends on target shift/model; alarms still do not establish mechanism.

sources.exact_title: The Economic Design of X Charts Used to Maintain Current Control of a Process
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 228–242
sources.claim_supported: Makes sampling interval, sample size and limits an explicit economic decision balancing false alarms, detection and operating costs.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct basis for P021 and P057.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Cost models can be misspecified and may omit catastrophic or ethical consequences.

sources.exact_title: Realistic Evaluation of the Precision and Accuracy of Instrument Calibration Systems
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 161–187; DOI 10.6028/JRES.067C.015
sources.claim_supported: Treats calibration as a measurement process requiring evidence of both statistical control and accuracy.
sources.relation_to_property: Foundational measurement-science support for P002–P007 and P010.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Calibration-system evaluation does not by itself validate the measurand or downstream decision threshold.

sources.exact_title: Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 73–101
sources.claim_supported: Develops estimation procedures with controlled sensitivity to contamination/model departures.
sources.relation_to_property: Robustness lineage for P040, P043, P055.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Robustness is relative to a contamination neighbourhood/loss; it cannot make an undefined construct valid.

sources.author_organisation: George E. P. Box and David R. Cox
sources.exact_title: An Analysis of Transformations
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 211–252
sources.claim_supported: Provides likelihood-based transformation methods and diagnostics for model form.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Transformation can improve fit without repairing dependence, selection bias or construct invalidity.

sources.exact_title: Estimating Causal Effects of Treatments in Randomized and Nonrandomized Studies
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 688–701
sources.claim_supported: Clarifies potential outcomes, assignment mechanisms and the role of randomisation for causal estimation.
sources.relation_to_property: Causal-design ancestry for P029–P031 and P039–P040.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Randomisation identifies effects for the actual assignment/units under assumptions; it does not ensure transport or no interference.

sources.exact_title: Problems of Monetary Management: The U.K. Experience
sources.date_version_edition: 1975; Papers in Monetary Economics, Reserve Bank of Australia
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: pp. 1–20; passage later termed Goodhart’s law
sources.claim_supported: Observes that a statistical regularity can break down when used for control.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Originally a monetary-policy observation, not a universal formal law; generalisation requires mechanism.

sources.exact_title: Inference and Missing Data
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 581–592; ignorability conditions
sources.claim_supported: Classifies missingness mechanisms and states conditions under which likelihood/Bayesian inference may ignore them.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: MAR/ignorability are assumptions about unseen data and parameter distinctness, not facts established by software defaults.

sources.exact_title: Science and Statistics
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 791–799
sources.claim_supported: Presents iterative model criticism and the provisional nature of statistical models.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Iteration can become post-hoc flexibility unless data reuse and stopping are controlled.

sources.exact_title: Assessing the Impact of Planned Social Change
sources.date_version_edition: 1979; Evaluation and Program Planning 2(1):67–90; earlier 1976 paper
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 67–90; section on corruption of quantitative indicators
sources.claim_supported: Explains how high-stakes use can corrupt indicators and the processes they monitor.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Evidence is strongest for social indicators; technical metrics require a domain-specific gaming mechanism.

sources.exact_title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 187–211
sources.claim_supported: Shows that treating non-independent observations as independent experimental replication invalidates inference.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Taxonomy arose in ecology; exact remedies vary by cluster/time/system structure.

sources.author_organisation: J. Martin Bland and Douglas G. Altman
sources.exact_title: Statistical Methods for Assessing Agreement Between Two Methods of Clinical Measurement
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 307–310
sources.claim_supported: Shows correlation is inadequate for assessing agreement and proposes difference-based analysis.
sources.relation_to_property: Measurement agreement support for P008 and P053.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Limits of agreement are context- and heteroscedasticity-sensitive and do not establish validity.

sources.author_organisation: George E. P. Box, Søren Bisgaard and Conrad Fung
sources.exact_title: An Explanation and Critique of Taguchi’s Contributions to Quality Engineering
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 123–131
sources.claim_supported: Separates valuable robust-design ideas from statistical inefficiencies and overgeneralised signal-to-noise methods.
sources.relation_to_property: Critical evidence for P043 and P065.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Critique does not erase Taguchi’s influence or the value of designing insensitivity to noise factors.

sources.author_organisation: Layth C. Alwan and Harry V. Roberts
sources.exact_title: Time-Series Modeling for Statistical Process Control
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 87–95
sources.claim_supported: Demonstrates time-series approaches for autocorrelated process data.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Residual monitoring can hide model misspecification and may lose direct interpretability.

sources.exact_title: Measurement Invariance, Factor Analysis and Factorial Invariance
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 525–543
sources.claim_supported: Formalises invariance conditions needed to compare latent measurements across groups/contexts.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Latent-variable invariance is only one form of transport/construct stability and relies on model specification.

sources.exact_title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 289–300
sources.claim_supported: Introduces FDR control as an alternative error criterion for multiple testing.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: FDR control is not familywise control and depends on the procedure/dependence structure; it does not cure selective question formation.

sources.author_organisation: Douglas G. Altman and J. Martin Bland
sources.exact_title: Absence of Evidence Is Not Evidence of Absence
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full note, p. 485
sources.claim_supported: Explains why a non-significant result does not establish no effect.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for P036 and equivalence reasoning.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A brief note; formal equivalence/noninferiority designs supply stronger operational detail.

sources.author_organisation: William H. Woodall and Douglas C. Montgomery
sources.exact_title: Research Issues and Ideas in Statistical Process Control
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 376–386
sources.claim_supported: Surveys unresolved SPC research including assumptions, autocorrelation, multivariate and implementation issues.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A research agenda, not empirical validation of each proposed extension.

sources.exact_title: Controversies and Contradictions in Statistical Process Control
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 341–350
sources.claim_supported: Documents disputes over foundations, chart interpretation, probability models and practice.
sources.relation_to_property: Adversarial support for P015–P024 and P059.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Controversy does not imply control charts lack value; it narrows claims and requires context.

sources.author_organisation: K. W. Linna and William H. Woodall
sources.exact_title: Effect of Measurement Error on Shewhart Control Charts
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 213–222
sources.claim_supported: Shows measurement error can materially reduce chart detection performance and examines repeated measurements under cost constraints.
sources.relation_to_property: Direct bridge between measurement integrity and P015–P021.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Repeated measurement helps only under identified error/cost conditions and can replicate bias.

sources.author_organisation: Ronald L. Wasserstein and Nicole A. Lazar
sources.exact_title: The ASA Statement on p-Values: Context, Process, and Purpose
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: six principles; pp. 129–133
sources.claim_supported: States that p-values do not measure hypothesis truth/effect importance and decisions should not rest only on a threshold.
sources.relation_to_property: Strong critical support for P036–P037 and P058.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The statement does not ban p-values and does not prescribe one universal replacement.

sources.author_organisation: Ronald L. Wasserstein, Allen L. Schirm and Nicole A. Lazar
sources.exact_title: Moving to a World Beyond “p < 0.05”
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full editorial, pp. 1–19
sources.claim_supported: Argues against bright-line significance declarations and for context, effect sizes, uncertainty and transparency.
sources.relation_to_property: Evolutionary support for P036–P038 and P058.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: This editorial was not an ASA policy statement; statisticians contest abandoning significance language universally.

sources.author_organisation: ASA President’s Task Force on Statistical Significance and Replicability
sources.exact_title: Task Force Statement on Statistical Significance and Replicability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: entire statement; paragraphs on uncertainty, thresholds, multiplicity and replicability
sources.claim_supported: Affirms properly applied p-values while requiring uncertainty, design, model choice, transparency, multiplicity and decision consequences.
sources.relation_to_property: Balanced contemporary disposition for P036–P038 and P058.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Rejects both ritual thresholding and blanket claims that p-values are intrinsically invalid.

sources.author_organisation: Steven R. Howard, Aaditya Ramdas, Jon McAuliffe and Jasjeet Sekhon
sources.exact_title: Time-Uniform, Nonparametric, Nonasymptotic Confidence Sequences
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 1055–1080; definition of confidence sequence and main bounds
sources.claim_supported: Develops intervals valid uniformly over time, enabling planned anytime-valid inference under stated conditions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Time-uniform validity does not make adaptively chosen outcomes, contaminated samples or dependent data harmless.

sources.author_organisation: Ramesh Johari, Pete Koomen, Leonid Pekelis and David Walsh
sources.exact_title: Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 1806–1821
sources.claim_supported: Develops always-valid p-values/confidence intervals for continuously monitored online experiments.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Requires protocol/model conditions; operational deployment and effect heterogeneity remain separate problems.

sources.author_organisation: Cynthia Dwork, Vitaly Feldman, Moritz Hardt, Toniann Pitassi, Omer Reingold and Aaron Roth
sources.exact_title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 636–638; reusable-holdout mechanism
sources.claim_supported: Shows adaptive reuse of holdout data can invalidate ordinary guarantees and gives a privacy-based correction.
sources.relation_to_property: Modern domain support for P054 and P051–P052.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The mechanism is not a universal cure for benchmark contamination or construct drift.

sources.author_organisation: Benjamin Recht, Rebecca Roelofs, Ludwig Schmidt and Vaishaal Shankar
sources.exact_title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full paper, pp. 5389–5400; new test-set construction and results
sources.claim_supported: Finds material accuracy drops on newly collected test sets despite preserved relative progress, illustrating distribution/benchmark sensitivity.
sources.relation_to_property: Modern domain evidence for P049, P051 and P054.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Relative gains transferred better than absolute scores, so benchmark reuse did not erase all comparative information.

sources.author_organisation: Joseph P. Simmons, Leif D. Nelson and Uri Simonsohn
sources.exact_title: False-Positive Psychology: Undisclosed Flexibility in Data Collection and Analysis Allows Presenting Anything as Significant
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Experiments 1–2 and simulation; pp. 1359–1366
sources.claim_supported: Demonstrates how analyst degrees of freedom inflate false positives.
sources.relation_to_property: Empirical support for P037, P038 and P052.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Psychology examples do not quantify every engineering workflow; the mechanism is general only where similar flexibility exists.

sources.exact_title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 355–362
sources.claim_supported: Explains equivalence testing against a smallest effect size of interest.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Requires a defensible equivalence margin and adequate design; it does not prove literal equality.

sources.exact_title: Statistical Tests, P Values, Confidence Intervals, and Power: A Guide to Misinterpretations
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 337–350; 25 misconceptions
sources.claim_supported: Catalogues common inferential misinterpretations and their corrections.
sources.relation_to_property: Critical support for P028, P036–P038, P058 and P063.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Tutorial evidence; does not choose a single decision framework for all engineering contexts.

sources.exact_title: A Glossary of DOE Terminology
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §5.7 entries for randomization, replication, blocking, confounding, resolution, response surface
sources.claim_supported: Defines core DOE concepts and distinctions used in industrial experimentation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Definitions do not guarantee good operationalisation or independent units.

sources.exact_title: Process Improvement
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Ch. 5; especially §§5.1–5.6 on DOE assumptions, design choice, analysis, screening, response surfaces and confirmation
sources.claim_supported: Presents designed experimentation as a structured route to valid, defensible and efficient process-learning conclusions, with explicit measurement, stability and model assumptions.
sources.relation_to_property: Current engineering support for P029–P035 and P041.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Handbook procedures are conditional on experimental-unit, model, randomisation, measurement and process assumptions.

sources.exact_title: The Data Are Randomly Sampled from the Process
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §4.2.1.5, especially “Data Must Reflect the Process” and “Data Best Reflects the Process Via Unbiased Sampling”
sources.claim_supported: Explains why representative process data are a precondition for valid modelling and why random sampling controls collection bias on average.
sources.relation_to_property: Current support for P025 and P028.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Random sampling cannot guarantee any particular sample is representative, and probability sampling may be infeasible in some engineering settings.

sources.exact_title: Sample Sizes Required
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: sample-size sections indexed through §7 and process-comparison chapters
sources.claim_supported: Relates sample size to alpha, beta/power, variation and the minimum meaningful effect.
sources.relation_to_property: Current support for P028 and P036.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Formulae do not rescue biased sampling, dependence or uncertain variance/effect assumptions.

sources.author_organisation: Michael G. Hudgens and M. Elizabeth Halloran
sources.exact_title: Toward Causal Inference with Interference
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 832–842
sources.claim_supported: Extends causal estimands/design reasoning when one unit’s treatment affects another.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Requires a specified interference structure; arbitrary network spillovers remain difficult.

sources.author_organisation: Byron Jones and Michael G. Kenward
sources.exact_title: Design and Analysis of Cross-Over Trials
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. 2–4 on design, period, sequence and carryover; later analysis chapters
sources.claim_supported: Treats carryover, period and sequence effects in repeated-treatment experiments.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Crossover efficiency can collapse when carryover/washout assumptions fail.

sources.author_organisation: George E. P. Box, J. Stuart Hunter and William G. Hunter
sources.exact_title: Statistics for Experimenters: Design, Innovation, and Discovery
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Parts I–IV; factorials, blocking, sequential experimentation and response surfaces
sources.claim_supported: Synthesises iterative industrial experimentation and graphical/model criticism.
sources.relation_to_property: Strong practice support for P030–P035 and P040–P041.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Textbook authority is not causal evidence that every formal DOE pays off in every low-cost setting.

sources.exact_title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: chapters on factorial/fractional factorial, blocking, RSM, robust parameter design
sources.claim_supported: Current industrial DOE synthesis.
sources.relation_to_property: Practice support across P029–P035 and P043.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A textbook tool menu can become ceremonial if the decision and cheapest discriminator are not specified first.

sources.author_organisation: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM)
sources.exact_title: Evaluation of Measurement Data—Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (JCGM 100:2008)
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Clauses 3–8 and Annexes; uncertainty evaluation and reporting
sources.claim_supported: Provides a general framework for identifying, combining and reporting measurement uncertainty components.
sources.relation_to_property: Measurement-science foundation for P007 and P002–P006.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A complete uncertainty budget does not by itself prove traceability, construct validity or decision usefulness.

sources.author_organisation: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM)
sources.exact_title: International Vocabulary of Metrology—Basic and General Concepts and Associated Terms (VIM), JCGM 200:2012
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: entries for measurand, calibration, metrological traceability, accuracy, precision, repeatability, reproducibility
sources.claim_supported: Supplies controlled distinctions among central measurement concepts.
sources.relation_to_property: Measurement-science basis for P001–P007 and P010–P011.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Definitions do not establish that a particular measurement system meets them.

sources.author_organisation: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM)
sources.exact_title: Evaluation of Measurement Data—The Role of Measurement Uncertainty in Conformity Assessment (JCGM 106:2012)
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Clauses 4–9, especially decision rules, guard bands and consumer/producer risks
sources.claim_supported: Connects uncertainty and decision rules to false acceptance/rejection in conformity assessment.
sources.relation_to_property: Strong support for P006–P007, P017, P052.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Guard bands require chosen loss/risk tolerances; they do not make poor specifications valid.

sources.exact_title: NIST Policy on Metrological Traceability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: definitions and policy sections on an unbroken calibration chain and stated uncertainty
sources.claim_supported: Clarifies traceability as a property of a measurement result, not a blanket property of an organisation or instrument.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: NIST explicitly warns traceability alone does not guarantee fitness for purpose or freedom from mistakes.

sources.exact_title: Measurement Process Characterization
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Ch. 2; repeatability/reproducibility, calibration, uncertainty and check standards
sources.claim_supported: Treats measurement as a process requiring characterisation, control and uncertainty evaluation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Methods assume suitable reference artefacts and do not define the construct being measured.

sources.exact_title: ISO/IEC 17025:2017—General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Clauses 6–8; resources, metrological traceability, methods, validity of results, records
sources.claim_supported: Requires competence, method validation, traceability where applicable, uncertainty and quality assurance for laboratory results.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Compliance/certification is not proof that a specific result is valid for an unstated decision.

sources.exact_title: ISO 5725-2:2025—Accuracy (Trueness and Precision) of Measurement Methods and Results—Part 2: Basic Method for the Determination of Repeatability and Reproducibility of a Standard Measurement Method
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Clauses 1–8 and annexes on collaborative interlaboratory precision experiments, repeatability and reproducibility estimation
sources.claim_supported: Specifies a collaborative interlaboratory design and analysis for estimating repeatability and reproducibility of a standard continuous-scale measurement method.
sources.relation_to_property: Current standards support for P005 and P008.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Its balanced interlaboratory method assumes standardised routine use, suitable materials and an approximately normal precision model; it does not establish construct validity.

sources.exact_title: Gauge R & R Studies
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §2.4 and subsections on study issues, design, data collection, repeatability, reproducibility, stability, bias and uncertainty
sources.claim_supported: Characterises gauges and production measurement systems by separating repeatability, reproducibility, stability and bias-related effects across artefacts, operators, gauges and configurations.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for P002, P005, P008 and P053.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Estimated components depend on the sampled parts, operators, gauges, configurations and range; fixed percentage cut-offs can become decision-detached ritual.

sources.author_organisation: Patrick E. Shrout and Joseph L. Fleiss
sources.exact_title: Intraclass Correlations: Uses in Assessing Rater Reliability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 420–428
sources.claim_supported: Distinguishes ICC forms according to rater sampling and agreement/consistency targets.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: ICC choice is design-dependent and reliability does not establish validity.

sources.author_organisation: NIST Office of Weights and Measures
sources.exact_title: Recommended Standard Operating Procedure for a Process Measurement Assurance Program
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: SOP 30 §§1–2 and sections on check-standard selection, charting, uncertainty and ongoing surveillance
sources.claim_supported: Shows how suitable check standards can monitor a calibration or measurement process over time and contribute evidence about capability, bias, drift and uncertainty.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A check standard is a surrogate: it must be stable and representative enough, and its success does not establish validity for unrepresented workloads or contexts.

sources.exact_title: Process or Product Monitoring and Control
sources.claim_supported: Provides current control-chart, acceptance-sampling, capability and time-series guidance.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Handbook methods are not permission to ignore assumptions or use charts as universal dashboards.

sources.exact_title: What Is Process Capability?
sources.claim_supported: Defines capability as comparison of an in-control process with specifications and states distribution/sample assumptions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Capability indices can mislead for unstable, dependent, non-normal or poorly measured processes.

sources.exact_title: ISO 22514-1:2014—Statistical Methods in Process Management—Capability and Performance—Part 1: General Principles and Concepts
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: general principles, terminology, study circumstances and acceptance/improvement uses
sources.claim_supported: Standardises the general principles and decision contexts for process capability and performance studies.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Use of the standard does not establish that the process, measurement system, distributional model or future operating regime satisfies the study prerequisites.

sources.exact_title: ISO 22514-2:2026—Statistical Methods in Process Management—Capability and Performance—Part 2: Process Capability and Performance of Time-Dependent Process Models
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: scope and clauses on time-dependent process models/stability
sources.claim_supported: Updates capability practice for time-dependent behaviour rather than assuming fixed iid output.
sources.relation_to_property: Current evolutionary support for P019 and P022.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Model choice remains consequential; a standard cannot guarantee adequate modelling.

sources.exact_title: Statistical Quality Control Handbook
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: control-chart pattern rules and interpretation chapters
sources.claim_supported: Popularised supplementary run rules beyond single three-sigma limits.
sources.relation_to_property: Historical basis for run-rule practice in P021/P059.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Multiple rules shorten in-control average run length and raise false-alarm burden.

sources.exact_title: The 100th Anniversary of the Control Chart
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 2–4; centenary historical synthesis
sources.claim_supported: Reviews the control chart’s Bell Labs origin, enduring role and evolution across a century.
sources.relation_to_property: Historical/current synthesis for P015–P021 and the timeline.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A short centenary review does not eliminate disputes about probabilistic foundations or domain transfer.

sources.exact_title: Introduction to Time Series Analysis
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §6.4, especially the distinction between ordinary process monitoring and data with autocorrelation, trend or seasonality
sources.claim_supported: Explains that serial dependence, trend and seasonality create internal time structure that must be modelled rather than treated as independent observations.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Time-series adjustment can still miss structural breaks, changing mixtures or model failure; process knowledge remains necessary.

sources.exact_title: What Is Acceptance Sampling?
sources.claim_supported: Defines acceptance sampling as lot disposition rather than quality estimation and lists contexts such as destructive or costly inspection.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: It can protect transactions without improving the producing process.

sources.exact_title: ISO 2859-1:2026—Sampling Procedures for Inspection by Attributes—Part 1: Sampling Schemes Indexed by Acceptance Quality Limit (AQL) for Lot-by-Lot Inspection
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: scope; AQL-indexed single, double, multiple, sequential and skip-lot procedures and switching rules
sources.claim_supported: Provides current lot-by-lot attribute-sampling schemes indexed by AQL, with switching and alternative plan structures.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: AQL is not a guarantee for an individual lot or a desired process defect rate, and lot disposition is not process improvement.

sources.exact_title: ISO 28590:2017—Sampling Procedures for Inspection by Attributes—Introduction to the ISO 2859 Series of Standards for Sampling for Inspection by Attributes
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: scope, series overview and guidance on selecting an inspection system
sources.claim_supported: Introduces the ISO 2859 family, summarises its attribute-sampling schemes and guides selection for a stated inspection situation.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for the proper scope of P026–P027.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: It does not turn acceptance sampling into process improvement, quality estimation or causal diagnosis.

sources.exact_title: Assessing Product Reliability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Ch. 8, including life distributions, censoring, ALT, repair models and growth
sources.claim_supported: Provides engineering reliability methods and assumptions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Handbook methods depend on failure definitions, sampling, models and test-use equivalence.

sources.exact_title: Accelerated Life Tests
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §8.3.1.4 and acceleration-model subsections
sources.claim_supported: Explains why ALT is used when use-stress tests yield few failures and requires acceleration/life-distribution models.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: High-stress failure modes may differ; extrapolation can be fragile.

sources.exact_title: Constant Repair Rate (HPP/Exponential) Model
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §8.4.5.1, especially the zero-failure MTBF lower-bound and confidence-limit discussion
sources.claim_supported: Under a homogeneous-Poisson/exponential repair model, zero observed failures yields only a one-sided lower bound on MTBF rather than proof of a zero failure rate.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The result is conditional on constant repair rate, exposure accounting and model adequacy; it is not a general nonparametric guarantee for every reliability claim.

sources.exact_title: Tolerance Intervals for a Normal Distribution
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §7.2.6.3, especially the distinction among tolerance intervals, confidence intervals and engineering tolerances
sources.claim_supported: Defines intervals intended to cover a stated population proportion with stated confidence and distinguishes them from parameter confidence intervals and design specifications.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: This construction assumes a normal population; small samples and tail claims are highly assumption-sensitive.

sources.author_organisation: John A. Hanley and Abby Lippman-Hand
sources.exact_title: If Nothing Goes Wrong, Is Everything All Right? Interpreting Zero Numerators
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 1743–1745; rule-of-three argument
sources.claim_supported: Shows zero observed events still permits a nonzero upper failure-rate bound.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Simple approximation assumes independent Bernoulli opportunities and does not handle exposure heterogeneity.

sources.exact_title: Accelerated Testing: Statistical Models, Test Plans, and Data Analyses
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Parts I–IV on acceleration models, planning, censored data and analysis
sources.claim_supported: Comprehensive technical basis for ALT design and extrapolation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Model adequacy and physical failure-mechanism continuity remain empirical burdens.

sources.author_organisation: William Q. Meeker and Luis A. Escobar
sources.exact_title: Statistical Methods for Reliability Data
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: chapters on censored life data, regression, acceleration and prediction
sources.claim_supported: Treats censored reliability data and uncertainty in lifetime prediction.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Sophisticated modelling cannot overcome unrepresentative duty cycles or changed failure mechanisms.

sources.exact_title: Reliability Growth: Enhancing Defense System Reliability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. 2–5; assumptions and limits of growth models/test programmes
sources.claim_supported: Assesses reliability growth and warns that changing environments/configurations complicate trend attribution.
sources.relation_to_property: Critical support for P046 and P049.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Defence acquisition context is domain-specific; not every conclusion transfers.

sources.exact_title: Explore Statistical Engineering
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: official definition and problem-characterisation paragraphs
sources.claim_supported: Defines statistical engineering as structuring and solving large, complex, unstructured problems requiring data and multiple disciplines.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: An emerging disciplinary definition is not proof of unique methods or programme-wide causal payoff.

sources.author_organisation: Roger W. Hoerl and Ronald D. Snee
sources.exact_title: Statistical Engineering: An Idea Whose Time Has Come?
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 209–219; theory/definition and complex-problem discussion
sources.claim_supported: Argues that integrating statistical science, tools and other disciplines is needed for large unstructured problems.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Conceptual theory and cases do not establish a universal branded methodology.

sources.author_organisation: Stefan H. Steiner and R. Jock MacKay
sources.exact_title: Statistical Engineering: An Algorithm for Reducing Variation in Manufacturing Processes
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full book; variation-reduction algorithm and case studies
sources.claim_supported: Presents a manufacturing-specific diagnostic/remedial algorithm for variation reduction.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: This is a narrower use of “statistical engineering” than the later ISEA discipline.

sources.author_organisation: Roger G. Schroeder, Kevin Linderman, Charles Liedtke and Adrian S. Choo
sources.exact_title: Six Sigma: Definition and Underlying Theory
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 536–554
sources.claim_supported: Finds Six Sigma’s tools resemble prior quality methods while its distinctive contribution is an organisational role/project/metaroutine structure.
sources.relation_to_property: Evidence for separating programme artefacts P060–P062 from underlying properties.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Grounded organisational theory is not proof that each deployment causes superior outcomes.

sources.author_organisation: Jeroen de Mast and Joran Lokkerbol
sources.exact_title: An Analysis of the Six Sigma DMAIC Method from the Perspective of Problem Solving
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 604–614
sources.claim_supported: Analyses DMAIC as a generic problem-solving structure and distinguishes types of problems/tools.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for P061 as programme translation rather than unique property.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Phase structure can aid coordination but is neither necessary nor sufficient for valid evidence.

sources.author_organisation: Michael Sony, Jiju Antony, Sung Park and Michael Mutingi
sources.exact_title: Key Criticisms of Six Sigma: A Systematic Literature Review
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full review, pp. 950–962; 61 articles and 12 criticism themes
sources.claim_supported: Systematically documents implementation, rigidity, innovation, resource, evidence and other criticisms of Six Sigma.
sources.relation_to_property: Critical evidence for P060–P062 and ceremony stripping.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Criticism literature is heterogeneous and does not show underlying statistical mechanisms are invalid.

sources.author_organisation: Morgan Swink and Brian W. Jacobs
sources.exact_title: Six Sigma Adoption: Operating Performance Impacts and Contextual Drivers of Success
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: event-study/firm analysis, pp. 437–453
sources.claim_supported: Reports associations/market-operating effects around adoption and examines contextual drivers.
sources.relation_to_property: Empirical programme evidence, separated from tool validity.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Observational adoption studies face selection, timing and concurrent-change confounding.

sources.author_organisation: Scott M. Shafer and Susan B. Moeller
sources.exact_title: The Effects of Six Sigma on Corporate Performance: An Empirical Investigation
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 521–532; structural/archival analysis
sources.claim_supported: Examines mechanisms and performance associations of Six Sigma programmes.
sources.relation_to_property: Empirical programme evidence for ceremony-vs-property assessment.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Causal attribution remains weaker than formal/tool evidence and may depend on implementation context.

sources.author_organisation: Joshua R. Vest and Lisa D. Gamm
sources.exact_title: A Critical Review of the Research Literature on Six Sigma, Lean and StuderGroup’s Hardwiring Excellence in the United States
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article; methods, results and limitations sections
sources.claim_supported: Finds limited and methodologically weak evidence for healthcare quality-improvement brands relative to claims.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Healthcare implementation differs from manufacturing and later evidence has expanded.

sources.exact_title: What Deming Told the Japanese in 1950
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 9–24; analysis of authentic lecture transcripts
sources.claim_supported: Shows Deming’s 1950 Japanese lectures devoted substantial attention to statistical quality control.
sources.relation_to_property: Documented transmission evidence for Deming/Japan genealogy.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Does not support a single-hero account of Japanese quality development.

sources.exact_title: Out of the Crisis
sources.date_version_edition: 1986; MIT Press edition; lectures/book originated earlier
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Chs. 3, 8, 11 and 14 Points; discussion of variation, tampering and management responsibility
sources.claim_supported: Translates variation thinking into management, warns against numerical targets, tampering and blaming individuals for system causes.
sources.relation_to_property: Management-programme translation for P015, P020, P051, P057.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Later management philosophy exceeds the statistical mechanism and contains claims not independently established by control-chart theory.

sources.exact_title: Quality-Control Handbook
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Parts on quality planning, control, inspection and statistical methods
sources.claim_supported: Systematises managerial and engineering quality planning/control beyond a single statistical tool.
sources.relation_to_property: Quality ancestry for P056 and programme distinctions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Handbook authority does not make every later Juran-branded practice a general statistical property.

sources.exact_title: The Quality Trilogy
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 19–24
sources.claim_supported: Distinguishes quality planning, control and improvement as different managerial processes.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The trilogy is an organisational framing, not an inferential guarantee.

sources.author_organisation: Union of Japanese Scientists and Engineers (JUSE)
sources.exact_title: The Deming Prize: History and Guide
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: history/timeline sections
sources.claim_supported: Documents institutionalisation of quality control and the Deming Prize in Japan.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Official history may emphasise institutional narrative; it does not isolate causal contributions.

sources.exact_title: Statistical Quality Control and the Deming Legacy
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 8–11
sources.claim_supported: Challenges oversimplified accounts of Deming as sole source of Japanese quality success.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A short historical essay; detailed transmission claims require primary records.

sources.exact_title: Quality Engineering Using Robust Design
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: chapters on parameter design, noise factors, S/N ratios and confirmation
sources.claim_supported: Documents Taguchi-derived robust-design practice in US engineering.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Some recommended analyses and S/N ratios were criticised as inefficient or condition-specific.

sources.exact_title: Taguchi’s Parameter Design: A Panel Discussion
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full panel, pp. 127–161
sources.claim_supported: Preserves both contributions and disagreements over Taguchi parameter design and analysis.
sources.relation_to_property: Balanced evidence for P043 and P065.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: No single consensus that all Taguchi procedures are optimal.

sources.author_organisation: Ramón V. León, Angela C. Shoemaker and Raghu N. Kackar
sources.exact_title: Performance Measures Independent of Adjustment: An Explanation and Extension of Taguchi’s Signal-to-Noise Ratios
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 253–265
sources.claim_supported: Identifies conditions and alternatives for separating adjustment from dispersion performance.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: S/N measures remain tied to particular mean-variance structures and objectives.

sources.exact_title: Improving Ratings: Audit in the British University System
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 305–321; audit/target discussion
sources.claim_supported: Explains how measures used as targets can alter behaviour and lose informational value.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Higher-education audit is not direct lineage to industrial quality control.

sources.exact_title: Information Value Theory
sources.date_version_edition: 1966; IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics 2(1):22–26
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 22–26
sources.claim_supported: Formalises the value of information relative to a decision and utility.
sources.relation_to_property: Convergent decision-analysis support for P041 and P057.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Requires a credible decision model and utilities; information may have option/learning value not captured simply.

sources.author_organisation: Joaquin Quiñonero-Candela, Masashi Sugiyama, Anton Schwaighofer and Neil D. Lawrence, eds.
sources.exact_title: Dataset Shift in Machine Learning
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Parts I–IV on covariate, prior and concept shift and applications
sources.claim_supported: Systematises prediction under training/deployment distribution differences.
sources.relation_to_property: Modern domain translation for P049 and P009.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: ML shift taxonomies do not prove historical quality-engineering lineage or solve causal drift.

sources.exact_title: ISO/IEC Guide 98-4:2012—Uncertainty of Measurement—Part 4: Role of Measurement Uncertainty in Conformity Assessment
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: Clauses 4–9 and guard-band examples
sources.claim_supported: Normative publication of JCGM 106 decision-rule/uncertainty concepts.
sources.relation_to_property: Standards support for P006–P007, P017 and P052.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Conformance decisions remain conditional on specifications and loss/risk choices.

sources.exact_title: Detailed Table of Contents
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: indexed Chapters 1–8, especially measurement, modelling, DOE, monitoring, comparison and reliability sections
sources.claim_supported: Provides the stable section map used to locate the handbook’s measurement, modelling, DOE, monitoring, comparison and reliability guidance.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: An index supports navigation and locators but does not itself establish substantive claims.

sources.exact_title: Signal-to-Noise Ratios, Performance Criteria, and Transformations
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 1–17
sources.claim_supported: Shows common Taguchi S/N ratios are appropriate only under specific mean-variance/performance relationships.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The robust-design objective survives even when a particular criterion is rejected.

sources.author_organisation: Steven D. Phillips and Michael Krystek
sources.exact_title: Assessment of Conformity, Decision Rules and Risk Analysis
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: full article, pp. 237–245; decision-rule and risk-analysis sections
sources.claim_supported: Explains how measurement uncertainty and decision rules jointly determine false-accept and false-reject risks in conformity assessment.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for P006–P007, P017 and P052.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Risk parameters, guard bands and loss choices remain context-specific and cannot validate a poor specification.

sources.exact_title: Fitting Models Using Degradation Data Instead of Failures
sources.claim_supported: Shows degradation trajectories can support lifetime modelling before observed failures when linked to failure thresholds.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Extrapolation inherits degradation-model and threshold assumptions.

sources.exact_title: ISO/IEC 17043:2023—Conformity Assessment—General Requirements for the Competence of Proficiency Testing Providers
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: requirements for proficiency-testing schemes, assigned values, evaluation and reporting
sources.claim_supported: Supports external/interlaboratory checks of measurement competence.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Proficiency on provided samples may not establish routine-sample representativeness.

sources.exact_title: Statistical Process Control (SPC)
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: sections on common/special cause and control-chart purpose
sources.claim_supported: Summarises mainstream SPC interpretation and chart use.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Professional summary omits many model and transfer limitations.

sources.exact_title: What Are Variables Control Charts?
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §6.3.2 and subsections on X-bar/R/S, individuals, CUSUM and EWMA
sources.claim_supported: States control limits, distribution assumptions and alternative chart types.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Run rules and nominal limits have false-alarm costs; baseline contamination matters.

sources.exact_title: What Are Attributes Control Charts?
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: §6.3.3 and count/proportion subsections
sources.claim_supported: Gives count/proportion monitoring models and assumptions.
sources.relation_to_property: Support for P024 and rare-event caveats.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Poisson/binomial assumptions often fail under overdispersion, dependence or changing opportunity counts.

sources.exact_title: Assessing Process Stability
sources.claim_supported: Separates process stability assessment from model fitting/capability.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A finite stable-looking baseline cannot guarantee future stationarity.

sources.author_organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.exact_title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_locator: entire handbook and chapter-specific locators
sources.claim_supported: Integrates measurement, characterisation, DOE, monitoring, comparison and reliability methods with assumptions.
sources.relation_to_property: Broad current technical corpus for the synthesis.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A handbook is a tool repository; evolved statistical engineering requires decision framing and anti-ceremony selection beyond tool availability.
